hypotheses.reasoning: GET /search 503s originate in catalog-svc, not search-api (search-api logs 0 errors; it only logs WARN retries). At 09:34:34 catalog-svc-3 failed its liveness probe and restarted (#1552), dropping capacity to 3/4 until it was ready again at 09:35:09 (#1600). Shortly after, catalog-svc reported overload: inflight rose to 853 with request rate 3.2x baseline (#1672), and it began load-shedding GET /products/batch with 503 (#1645). search-api then retried 503s immediately with backoff disabled (#1594 attempt 2/4, #1665 retry 3/4 delay 0ms, #1683 attempt 4 of 4), multiplying load on the already-saturated catalog-svc. Retries exhausted, so web-bff returned 503 on /search (#1595 and later). The pattern of load staying high after the restart matches the 'not recovering' alert, which is consistent with the retry amplification sustaining the overload. The initial trigger is small (one instance restart) and the damage comes from the retry storm. The notification-path problems (notif-db lock wait timeouts #1331/#1471, template-svc statement timeouts #1355/#1534, legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts from status-poller) are real but affect /v1/notify and status polling, not the /search path, so they are likely a separate, concurrent issue and not the root cause of the search 503s.

Lock waits on notif-db UPDATE notifications caused template-svc statement timeouts and notification-svc read timeouts, leading to api-gateway 504s on /v1/notify. This is a real fault but appears to be off the /search path; search-api and catalog-svc show no dependency on notification services, so it is an unlikely root cause of the search 503s.

verdict.recommendedAction: 1) Immediately stop the search-api retry storm: enable exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries (currently immediate retries, 4 attempts) for CatalogClient.getBatch. 2) Restore catalog-svc capacity: confirm all 4 instances are healthy and ready, and investigate why catalog-svc-3 failed its liveness probe at 09:34:34. Consider scaling catalog-svc or temporarily raising admission limits. 3) Consider a short-term search degradation path (serve cached results from redis-cache) while catalog recovers. 4) Separately, investigate the notif-db lock contention on UPDATE notifications and the template-svc statement timeouts, which are impacting /v1/notify, and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts from status-poller (deprecated endpoint still polled)."}]
